# AGENTS.md

<!-- ib:standard:start — generated by @inbeat/standards, edit in ib-toolkit -->
## inBeat toolkit standard

Stack: Next.js App Router, TypeScript strict, React 19, Drizzle + Neon, Clerk, Sentry, Vercel, Bun.
Shared code comes from `@inbeat/*` (ui ships source via `transpilePackages`; core and next ship compiled JS). Never fork a toolkit
file into the app; change it in ib-toolkit.

### Before you build

- If "Product brief" under "This app" is empty, write the user's brief there first (problem,
  users, core flows), then build.
- Read the matching guide before the work, whatever tool you are: `.agents/skills/ib-ui/SKILL.md`
  (component catalog, UI rules) before any UI, `.agents/skills/ib-feature/SKILL.md` for a new
  feature, `.agents/skills/ib-toolkit/SKILL.md` for actions, routes, auth, env and rate limits.
- Read the version-matched Next.js docs in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before Next.js work.

### Two tiers

- **Required** (CI enforces): `@inbeat/config` presets (extend them: biome, tsconfig, dependency-cruiser, vitest; `ib check`
  enforces it), the action/route error contract,
  `securityHeaders()`, Sentry presets, rate limiting on public entry points, this block.
- **Opt-in**: `@inbeat/ui` blocks, extra layer rules.
- A deliberate departure is allowed when the app states it under **Deliberate deviations**
  in its own section of this file (what, why, owner). Undeclared drift is a bug.

### Layout

```
src/app/                    routes + composition; private pieces in _components/
src/features/<f>/actions/   "use server" mutations, one per file, via action()
src/features/<f>/queries/   server-only reads for Server Components
src/features/<f>/server/    domain commands and policies ("server-only", no "use server")
src/features/<f>/components/ hooks/ lib/ schemas.ts types.ts
src/entities/               leaf: domain types, zod schemas, constants
src/integrations/<vendor>/  external adapters
src/shared/{components,config,lib,hooks}/
src/db/schema/<table>.ts, src/db/migrations/
```

Layers (dependency-cruiser, `@inbeat/config/dependency-cruiser`): features never import each
other; entities import nothing internal; db imports entities only; shared and integrations never
import features or app.

### Reads and writes

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Page data | Server Component calls `queries/*` |
| Mutation from own UI | `action()` from `@inbeat/next/action`, returns `Result` |
| Client polling, infinite lists | `GET` via `route()`, React Query |
| Webhooks, presign, redirects, cron | `route()` |

Server actions are queued per client; never use them for reads.

### Errors

- Actions resolve to `{ ok: true, data } | { ok: false, error, code?, errorId? }`.
  Routes answer `{ error, code, errorId? }` with the status from `APP_ERROR_STATUS`.
- Throw `AppError(kind)` from `@inbeat/core/errors`; never `new Error("Forbidden")`.
  Kinds: validation, auth, forbidden, not_found, conflict, rate_limited, db_transient,
  db_query, timeout, external_service, unknown.
- Unexpected errors are classified, reported once, and replaced with safe copy + `ERR_xxxx`.
- Log with `createLogger()`; ids only, never emails, names or payloads. No `console.log`.

### Auth

- New apps start without authentication; set it up per "Integrations" in the `ib-toolkit` skill.
- `authorize` is required on every `action()` and `route()`, and it is the app's own check
  (session, roles, ownership). `publicAccess` is an explicit choice and must be rate limited.
- Redirect targets go through `safeRedirectPath`. `APP_URL` comes from env, never `Host`.

### Security baseline

- `securityHeaders()` in `next.config.ts`; CSP report-only until a clean week, then enforce.
- `createRateLimiter()` (Upstash in prod) on every unauthenticated entry, presign and LLM call.
- Webhooks verify the sender's signature. Secrets only in Vercel env.
- `import "server-only"` in every module touching secrets or the DB.
- Env through `@t3-oss/env-nextjs` + `@inbeat/core/env` fragments; no `process.env` elsewhere.

### Data

- UUID PKs, `timestamp({ withTimezone: true })`, snake_case, one table per file.
- Migrations are generated, reviewed, forward-only, expand then contract; they run after the
  build resolves. Never run migrations or destructive SQL against production unless the user
  says "apply migrations to prod".
- Deletes that own storage objects collect keys in the transaction and delete after commit.

### UI

- UI comes only from `@inbeat/ui` (catalog in the `ib-ui` skill) plus layouts composed from it. If a
  component or variant is missing, stop and flag it for ib-toolkit; never invent, copy or patch
  one (a workaround needs the user's OK and a `// toolkit-gap:` comment).
- Primitives and generic blocks from `@inbeat/ui/components/*`; tokens from
  `@inbeat/ui/theme.css`. A block moves to the toolkit only once an app actually uses it.
- Buttons are `rounded-full` with no destructive variant; destructive flows use
  `DestructiveActionDialog` from `@inbeat/ui`. Icon-only buttons get a tooltip. Lists use
  `DataTableShell` + `DataTable`; empty lists use `EmptyState`.
- Radix via `radix-ui`; animation via `motion` only.

### Simplicity

- Reuse before writing: the `ib-ui` catalog, `@inbeat/*`, the stdlib, then the platform. No speculative abstractions, config or "for later" scaffolding.
- Comments carry only what code cannot. A deliberate shortcut is marked `// shortcut: <ceiling>; <upgrade path>`.
- Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` only when the app has no `CLAUDE.md`; if one exists it must contain an `@AGENTS.md` line (`ib check` fails otherwise).

### Tests and CI

- Vitest colocated `*.test.ts` for every `server/` command, policy and `lib/` function;
  `*.integration.test.ts` against a Neon branch; Playwright in `tests/e2e` against previews.
- CI: biome, tsc, dependency-cruiser, vitest, migration check, `ib check`, gitleaks.
- Release: production holds on the Vercel Deployment Check `release`, set by the toolkit `release-gate.yml` after re-verifying (and migrating) the deployed commit.

### Commits

Conventional commits, lowercase, present tense, title under 60 chars. No AI attribution.
Never commit, push or open a PR unless explicitly asked.

## This app

### Product brief

- The Album + Misión Incógnita: a small game for an inBeat teammate's first two weeks, or anyone's
  who an admin turns a mission on for. "New hire" is not a kind of person: it is someone whose
  mission has not finished.
- Users: teammates (fill in their sticker card, collect stickers, write their three secret clues),
  players (a teammate with a mission), the secret welcomer (a teammate picked when a mission
  starts), admins (People Strategy).
- Core flows: every signed-in teammate has an album and collects stickers by chatting with people
  and writing one thing they learned (private notebook). Turning a mission on starts it: a random
  welcomer is picked and day 1 is today (there is no Start button and no waiting state). The
  player's first visit shows the welcome tour as an explanation, then leads to the mission. Four
  clues (day 3 is always the welcomer's team, days 6, 9, 12 are the welcomer's own, copied when the
  mission starts); guess any collected sticker, a wrong guess rules that person out; found or
  revealed on day 14; then the player makes their own sticker. Only a teammate with a complete card
  and all three clues written can be picked as a welcomer. The admin People page has three views, each person in
  exactly one by mission state: Playing, No mission (no game, signed in or not, with an icon
  until they sign in; search, filter, and select people to turn missions on; people who find no
  free welcomer stay here and the toast says so) and Done. A mission starts automatically when Deel reports a new hire active (see Auto-mission) or when an admin starts it: "Start as
  new hire" (No mission rows, confirmed first) flags the person and starts the mission at once (no
  free welcomer: the person stays flagged in No mission, and the toast says so), and Turn on starts
  the others, signed in or not. A running mission is ended with End mission only: it resets the game
  (guesses and clues cleared), keeps the album, notes and new hire flag, and starting again picks a
  new welcomer. One pipeline, the rite of passage: a new hire (`people.new_hire`,
  set by "Start as new hire", and cleared when their mission ends, found or revealed)
  earns their card and clues by playing. While the flag is set My card and My clues are hidden,
  /card and /clues redirect, and the card and clue actions refuse ("Finish your mission first.";
  one rule, `isLockedNewHire`). With no mission they have nothing to open, only the locked home.
  A teammate who is not a new hire keeps My card and My clues, mission or not, and is turned on
  from No mission once they can welcome (a complete card and all three clues).
- Design source: the canvas at https://claude.ai/artifact/9V2NQ7cHj3dC2rRtjs4ovj and `docs/plan.md`.

### Stack deltas

- Clerk with Sign in with Slack (phase 1). Access is strict: the verified email must match exactly one
  person, on `email` or `personal_email`; there is no domain allowlist.
- Drizzle + Neon (phase 1). Cloudflare R2 for photos (phase 3).
- Notifications leave the app as signed webhook events to n8n, which posts to Slack. No Slack API
  in the app.
- Playwright e2e against previews (phase 8).
- Storybook (`@storybook/nextjs-vite`) for the game UI kit: stories sit beside each component as
  `src/shared/components/game/*.stories.tsx`; run `bun run storybook` (port 6006) or
  `bun run build-storybook`. Stories share sample people with the dev catalogue through
  `src/shared/components/game/fixtures.ts`; add data there, never inline. The static build copies
  the licensed fonts from `public/fonts`, so never deploy `storybook-static` publicly.
- `@biomejs/biome` pinned to 2.5.15: Biome 2.6 formats markdown and rewrites the managed toolkit
  files, which then fails `ib check`. Unpin when ib-toolkit excludes markdown.

### Deliberate deviations

| What | Why | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Player and admin screens use a game UI layer in `src/shared/components/game` built on Fieldtrip tokens and fonts, not `@inbeat/ui` | The product is a game with the Fieldtrip brand, admin included | John |
| `canvas-confetti` for confetti, beside `motion` | Use an existing library instead of hand-built sparkle | John |
| PR-title lint and release-please in this app | Versioned releases and a changelog for the app | John |

### Known gaps

- Deel disables a webhook after 10 failed deliveries and nothing in the app notices. Every delivery
  logs `deel webhook` with the event type and outcome; no such log for days, or a new Deel hire
  missing, means re-enable it in Deel, Organization settings, Developer, Webhooks. Replay an event
  locally with `bun run deel:replay -- worker.v2.updated --id <deel person id>` (signs with
  `DEEL_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; `--url` targets a preview). There is no full sync: people missed while a
  webhook was down appear only on their next event or after another `deel:backfill`.
- The licensed Fieldtrip fonts in `public/fonts` are committed so previews render them, although the
  repo is public. Shortcut until the repo goes private or the fonts move to private storage fetched at
  build time; then re-add `/public/fonts/` to `.gitignore`. Owner: John.
- Sentry is wired by the template but has no project yet: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` stays empty until
  the owner creates one. Errors still get `ERR_xxxx` ids and logs.
- Only Clerk's development instance is set up. It signs in with Slack through a Slack app in the inBeat
  workspace (custom credentials): Clerk's shared Slack app is refused there with
  `invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app`. Still to do: the production instance, with its Redirect URL
  added to the same Slack app. Roles need the `{"metadata": "{{user.public_metadata}}"}` session
  claim and `{"role": "admin"}` in the user's public metadata; without them a user is `member`.
- No cron yet (phase 6): clue visibility and the day-14 reveal are computed on read, and an
  expired active game is ended as `revealed` by the first player or welcomer request after it
  (`// shortcut:` in `finalize-expired-game-record.ts`). No notifications are sent.
- Upstash is not set up: without `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` and `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` the rate
  limiter keeps per-instance memory counters and logs a warning.
- Sticker photos show initials until phase 3's signed R2 URL lands (`// shortcut:` in
  `to-sticker-person.ts`).

### Learned facts

- Players are not a Clerk role: a player is the `player` of a game, and a game is a person's one
  mission (unique per email and per player). Welcomers are the `welcomer` of a game. Clerk roles
  are only `admin` and `member`.
- The album belongs to the person: `collections` has `collector_person_id`, not a game, so
  deleting a game never touches it. Anyone signed in can open it; nobody collects their own sticker.
- A game exists only once its mission has started: `start_date` and the welcomer are set with the
  row (`welcomer_person_id` turns null only if the welcomer is later deleted; see the leavers fact).
  `beginMissionRecord` (used by turn-on and Start as new hire) takes one
  advisory lock, picks the welcomer, inserts the game with `start_date` today and copies the
  welcomer's three `welcomer_clues` into the per-game `clues` table; the board and the reveal read
  that copy. A partial unique index allows one active game per welcomer; a lost race is retried
  once, then answers "No welcomer is free right now. Try again tomorrow." Bulk turn-on starts people
  one by one and returns `{ started, skippedNoWelcomer }`. `games.player_person_id` is always set, signed in
  or not (people rows come from Deel); `games.player_email` is a legacy column, written but never
  read to find a game. `games.intro_seen_at` records the
  welcome tour, shown on the first visit to `/`.
- `getViewerPerson()` finds the viewer's `people` row by Clerk user id, else links the one row whose
  `email` or `personal_email` equals the verified primary email. It never creates a row: no match,
  or more than one, redirects to `/not-on-the-list`. A row already linked to another Clerk user is never moved; an admin clears `clerk_user_id` first.
  Once per Clerk session (`synced_session_id`) it re-reads the Clerk user for the Slack user id and
  the Slack photo, so a photo changed in Slack shows after the next sign-in.
- Emails (`people.email`, `games.player_email`) are stored normalized with `normalizeEmail`.
- Deel is the source of truth for who exists (`src/integrations/deel`, read-only client). Env:
  `DEEL_API_URL` (defaults to production), `DEEL_API_TOKEN` (people:read) and `DEEL_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
  (both required when `VERCEL_ENV` is `production`, optional elsewhere; without the secret the
  webhook answers 401) and the optional `DEEL_ORGANIZATION_ID`.
  `bun run deel:backfill` (dry run by default; `--apply`, plus `--confirm-production` against the
  production API) creates people and marks those already `active` with `auto_mission_done_at`, so
  they never auto-start; it runs `seedTeams` first. `people.deel_id` is the key; the work email
  fills `email`, a personal email `personal_email`; the Deel country is written to `location` and
  the hire date to `start_date`. `POST /api/webhooks/deel` verifies `x-deel-signature` (hex
  HMAC-SHA256 of `"POST"` plus the raw body), takes the person from the event, re-fetches them from
  Deel and classifies the change (`toRosterChange`): upsert, remove (leaver, below) or ignore. It
  handles `worker.v2.created|updated|deleted`, `employee.created.*`, `contract.status.updated`
  and `contract.terminated`; `onboarding.status.updated` is harmless and not a trigger.
  Responses: 401 bad or missing signature, 429 rate limited, 200 for ignored, unhandled and
  permanent outcomes (logged), 5xx only for transient failures so Deel retries. A replay only
  re-syncs current state.
- Auto-mission: after any upsert, a person whose Deel `hiring_status` is `active`, with
  `auto_mission_done_at` null, no game and a `start_date` within the last 30 days (`joinedRecently`),
  is flagged `new_hire` and `startAutoMissionRecord` starts
  their mission. `beginMissionRecord` sets the marker for every start, so End mission never
  restarts it. No free welcomer: the person stays flagged and unmarked until a later event or an
  admin starts them. A person who is not a recent hire is never flagged.
- A Deel department that maps to no team keeps the existing team and logs a warning with the Deel and
  department ids only.
- "Joined recently" (`joinedRecently`, `entities/game-schedule.ts`): `people.start_date` is at most
  30 days back in Montréal, or still ahead. No Mission rows show it as their small line.
- There is no Remove person: Deel decides who exists. `removeLeaverRecord` runs when a webhook's
  re-fetched Deel person is a leaver (`toRosterChange`): a 404, `inactive`, or `no_active_contracts` with an
  end date before today in Montréal. Any other answer, a 400 included, or no end date keeps them. In one transaction behind the mission-start lock it
  deletes the running game they welcome (its player stays flagged, `auto_mission_done_at` is cleared
  and `people.welcomer_left_at` is set, so People shows "Their welcomer left. Start them again." until
  `beginMissionRecord` clears it), deletes the game they play (also a legacy one found by `player_email`), then the `people` row (albums, their
  sticker in others' albums, notes and `welcomer_clues` cascade). Finished games they welcomed stay:
  `games.welcomer_person_id` is `set null` and the reveal reads the welcomer snapshot
  (`games.welcomer_name`, `welcomer_team_name`, `welcomer_image_url`, written at start). Their guess
  rows go with the person (accepted). The Clerk user stays and signing in is refused until Deel lists
  them again.
- The game runs on Montréal time (`America/Toronto`): day 1 is `games.start_date`, clues land at
  09:00 on days 3, 6, 9 and 12, the reveal at 09:00 on day 14 (`entities/game-schedule.ts`).
  Clue 1 is generated from the welcomer's team; clues 2 to 4 are the welcomer's own, one `welcomer_clues`
  row per (person, number), kept across missions. Teammates write them on `/clues`; `eligibleWelcomers`
  requires all three, and excludes the player, anyone welcoming a running mission and the person
  the player welcomes. While someone welcomes a started active mission their clues are read-only.
  Playing and welcoming at once is allowed.
- One top bar, `AppTopNav`, for every signed-in screen: tabs Album, Mission (only with a game in any state), My card, My clues, Welcomer (while welcoming a started mission), at most 5 in PillTabs; People (admins) is an icon button beside the avatar. Only pages everyone shown them can open become tabs.
- A card is complete only when team, location, fact and ask are all filled in (`isCardComplete` in
  `src/entities/card.ts`; `completeCardCondition` in `src/shared/lib` is the SQL twin: keep them in
  step). Album, welcomer pool and turn-on all use it. Name, team and location come from Deel and
  show read-only on /card; `updateMyCardSchema` and `updateCardRecord` write only fact and ask, so
  a payload with the others is stripped. An unmapped Deel department leaves the team null, so the
  card stays incomplete and the editor says "Your team isn't set yet. Ask People Strategy." The
  card saves while incomplete, after a confirm dialog: it leaves collectors' albums until
  completed (their `collections` rows stay). While someone welcomes a started mission
  (`findActiveWelcomerGame`) the server refuses a save that leaves the card incomplete, and clues
  are read-only.
- A blank clue text deletes that `welcomer_clues` row, so a clue is written or absent; a running
  mission keeps its own copy in `clues`.
- Player pages read through `loadPlayerBoard()` and the view shapers; never pass a raw `games`,
  `people` or `collections` row to a client component.
- Every player screen fills the viewport and centers its content vertically: `GameStage` always does it,
  there is no opt-in.
- `bun run db:seed:demo` builds a playable dev game (see the script header for the flags).
- Full-screen moments (card overlays, the reveal, the collect page) use the `screen-center` utility:
  a top bar with "The Album" logo lined up with `GameTopNav`'s, then the content centered on the
  screen itself. Actions sit centered under the content; no divider lines.
- Motion timing is shared from `src/shared/components/game/game-motion.ts` (durations, eases, `beats()`,
  `stagger()`, transitions) and content enters through `Reveal`; a feature's own choreography lives in a
  `*-motion.ts` file. `game-motion.test.ts` fails on inline timing literals and on CSS tokens that drift.
- Tooltips, player screens included, use `Tooltip` from `@inbeat/ui/components/tooltip` (text goes in
  `content`; `TooltipProvider` is mounted in the root layout). The trigger component must forward its
  props and ref, or the tooltip never opens.
- Teams are groups of Deel departments (all entities: IB, CM, CA, AAG), defined once in
  `src/entities/teams.ts`; the seeds and `teamForDeelDepartment` read that list. Renames go through
  `formerName` so `seedTeams` renames the row in place.
- Player-facing copy stays short and plain: one line telling the player what to do, no cute or
  wordy phrasing.
